::: notes
This last session takes apart the document on which the whole workshop leans, the report of the IDE workspace. It is a Quarto document, a file that holds prose and code together and becomes a finished report when it is rendered, running its code on the way. Every one of the workshop's workspaces has one, whatever its case study, and the one on my screen is the report of the Housing case study. We take it in four steps: what such a file holds and what rendering does to it; the header and the chunks of code, with the options that change what a chunk shows; the places where numbers, figures and references enter the text; and last a render from a clean session, which tests whether a report makes everything that it uses.
:::

# Source and output {#source-and-output .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Section 1
:::

::: notes
Section one is about the difference between a source and its output. A Quarto document is plain text, and we start with why that matters, then the three kinds of content that the file holds and the two programs that turn it into a report when you render it. Then we open the report of the IDE workspace in Positron, run its chunks one at a time in the console and preview the whole report, which is the first task of your own.
:::
